definitions.explanation: Used before a number of years to express how long ago a building was built. Almost exclusively seen in real estate listings: {築|ちく}10{年|ねん} = "built 10 years ago."

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦アパート→アパート：01012_apaato⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{築|ちく}10⟦{年|ねん}→年：09876_nen⟧だ。
{築|ちく}{浅|あさ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{物件|ぶっけん}→物件：06743_bukken⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{探|さが}している→探す：00493_sagasu⟧。
examples.english: I'm looking for a recently-built property.

examples.japanese: {築|ちく}50⟦{年|ねん}→年：09876_nen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{古民家|こみんか}→古民家：11833_kominka⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦リノベーション→リノベーション：11211_rinobeeshon⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{住|す}んでいる→住む：00673_sumu⟧。
examples.english: We renovated a 50-year-old traditional house and now live in it.

notes:
Derived from the verb ⟦{築|きず}く→築く：02046_kizuku⟧ (to build, to construct), but read ちく in this prefix usage. Appears in real estate listings and casual descriptions of a building's age. The fixed pattern is {築|ちく} + number + ⟦{年|ねん}→年：09876_nen⟧.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {築|ちく}〜⟦{年|ねん}→年：09876_nen⟧: built ~ years ago
- {築|ちく}{浅|あさ}: recently built (literally "newly built")
- {築|ちく}⟦{古|ふる}→古〜：03966_furu⟧: old building (less common but used in listings)
- ⟦{築|ちく}{年数|ねんすう}→築年数：17563_chikunensuu⟧: years since construction (the count itself)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{新築|しんちく}→新築：06567_shinchiku⟧: newly built — a building that has never been occupied
- ⟦{中古|ちゅうこ}→中古：03479_chuuko⟧: secondhand, used — for a previously-occupied property
- ⟦{古民家|こみんか}→古民家：11833_kominka⟧: traditional old house — typically 50+ years old, often with historic value
